root_cause_label: Agent misframed the task as 'make fasttext importable in all interpreters' rather than 'patch the NumPy 2.x incompatibility in FastText.py', and never ran the actual pytest to discover the real error, drifting into unnecessary multi-interpreter package installation instead of editing /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/FastText.py
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a false premise that the problem was interpreter/import mismatch rather than a NumPy API incompatibility bug in FastText.py source code, spending all steps installing fasttext across multiple interpreters while never patching np.array(probs, copy=False) to np.asarray(probs) as the task required.
t_err_evidence: At step 10, the agent pivots from diagnostics to attempting to install fasttext for /usr/bin/python3 (Python 3.11), acting on the false premise that the problem is that fasttext is not importable in all interpreters. This is the first action based on the wrong belief; the agent never ran pytest to identify the real failure (NumPy 2.x incompatibility in FastText.py), and misdiagnosed the task as an import/path issue.
t_commit_evidence: At step 16, the agent installs fasttext into the venv (Python 3.12) using uv, cementing a multi-interpreter installation strategy. By this point the agent is fully committed to making fasttext importable everywhere and there is no remaining chance it will pivot to patching FastText.py source code, given the subsequent verification steps (17, 23, 24, 27) all confirm the installations work.
trigger_explanation: The agent formed the false premise that the task's failure mode was 'fasttext not importable in certain Python interpreters' (based on the ModuleNotFoundError in the venv and Python 3.11). It never ran the actual pytest suite to discover the real error: a NumPy 2.x API breakage in FastText.py (np.array with copy=False parameter incompatibility). This false premise caused the entire fix strategy to be misdirected toward interpreter/package management instead of source code patching.
